articles.title: Ex-India captain Asunta Lakra leads protest against Hockey India officials
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former India women’s captain Asunta Lakra, along with a group of former national and international players, including Olympians, staged a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former India women’s captain Asunta Lakra, along with a group of former national and international players, including Olympians, staged a symbolic one-day protest against Hockey India secretary general Bholanath Singh and other office-bearers outside Gate No. 7 of the Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium here on Friday.The protesters, who had gathered at around 3pm, were also raising their voices against HI Director General Cdr R.K. Srivastava and treasurer Sekar J. Manoharan. The group demanded the formation of a sports ministry-backed ad-hoc committee to run the federation’s affairs until the next election.Asunta told TOI that the protest was initially planned at Jantar Mantar between 2pm and 4pm, but permission was denied by the police. The group subsequently assembled at the national stadium. Permission to protest at the main gate was also not granted, following which the protesters moved to Gate No. 7 and held their symbolic demonstration with placards before dispersing.The stadium complex houses offices of the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), including the Foreigners-I Division, Principal Accounts Office (Admn.) and Department of Border Management. Security at the premises is handled by the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), which was cited in connection with the denial of permission for a protest inside the complex.Those attending the demonstration included Olympians Ashok Kumar, Romeo James, Vineet Kumar and Manohar Topno. Romeo James and Vineet Kumar were members of the Indian team at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics. Asian Games medallist Pramod Batlaw, along with former international players Bimal Lakra, Kanti Baa and Birendra Lakra, were also present.Asunta has previously accused Bholanath Singh of intimidation and harassment after she raised objections over the alleged harassment of young girls in Jharkhand. Following her allegations, the Indian Olympic Committee (IOA) constituted a probe panel to look into the matter.The protesting group sought an ad-hoc committee to oversee the federation until the next elections. After staging the demonstration outside Gate No. 7, the group left the venue peacefully.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games: Anahat Singh, Abhay Singh lead India’s squash surge — two finals, three medals and Olympic spots in sight
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a remarkable day in squash at the Asian Games 2026 on Saturday, with Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh storming into the women’s and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a remarkable day in squash at the Asian Games 2026 on Saturday, with Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh storming into the women’s and men’s singles finals respectively, while the mixed doubles pairing of Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar secured a bronze medal at the Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena.The results gave India a shot at two squash gold medals on Sunday, while also putting Anahat and Abhay one victory away from potentially becoming India’s first squash players to secure direct qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.The Asian Games singles champions will earn direct LA28 qualification, subject to the eligibility criteria, including the PSA world ranking requirement at the qualification cut-off. Squash will make its Olympic debut in Los Angeles.It made Saturday one of the most productive days for Indian squash at a major continental event, with the country guaranteed three medals and still in contention for two golds.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleAnahat produces comeback for the agesThe biggest performance of the day came from 18-year-old Anahat, who pulled off one of the finest comebacks of her young career to defeat Japan's world No. 6 Satomi Watanabe 9-11, 11-13, 12-10, 11-6, 11-3.The world No. 17 Indian was staring at defeat after dropping the opening two games against the home favourite. Watanabe's variations, changes of pace and sharp angles had kept Anahat under constant pressure.But the teenager changed the complexion of the match in the third game.Trailing 8-10, Anahat saved two match points before producing a remarkable turnaround to win 12-10. She then carried the momentum into the fourth game, winning it 11-6 to level the contest.There was also an anxious moment during the semifinal when Anahat's head collided with Watanabe's shoulder while she attempted to retrieve the ball. The match was briefly stopped as the Indian received medical attention before returning to continue her fight.In the decider, Anahat gave Watanabe virtually no opportunity to regain control. She attacked with confidence and closed out the game 11-3 to complete a stunning 3-2 victory.The win was also revenge for Anahat, who had lost to Watanabe in another five-game contest earlier this year.Now she stands one victory away from an Asian Games gold medal — and potentially an Olympic ticket.Abhay follows Anahat into the gold-medal matchAbhay then completed India's singles double by powering past Pakistan's Muhammad Irfan 3-0 in the men's semifinal.The Indian won 11-3, 12-10, 11-6 in a 35-minute contest in which he controlled proceedings for long periods.Abhay made a fast start, racing to a 6-2 lead in the opening game before closing it out 11-3. Irfan pushed him harder in the second, but Abhay held his nerve in the tight moments to take it 12-10.There was no let-up in the third. Abhay maintained his control and closed out the match 11-6 to book his place in the final.Like Anahat, he is now one victory away from gold and a direct route to LA28. The Asian Games are the continental qualifying event for squash, with the men's and women's singles gold medallists earning Olympic qualification subject to the eligibility rules.Joshna and Velavan add a bronzeIndia's medal count in squash had already received a boost earlier in the day when Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar secured bronze in mixed doubles.The Indian pair lost a fiercely contested semifinal to Hong Kong's Tang Ming Hong and Lee Ka Yi 1-2 (10-11, 11-2, 10-11).After narrowly losing the opening game, Joshna and Velavan responded emphatically to level the contest by taking the second 11-2. The deciding game again went down to the wire, but the Hong Kong pair held their composure to win 11-10 and advance to the final.The bronze nevertheless marked another milestone for Joshna. Competing at a record seventh Asian Games, the 40-year-old added another medal to a collection that already included two silver and three bronze medals at the continental showpiece.India had assured itself of the mixed doubles medal after Joshna and Velavan defeated the Philippines' David Pelino and Jemyca Aribado in the quarterfinals on Friday.But Saturday's bigger story was the singles double.With Anahat and Abhay both through to the finals, India now has two chances to win squash gold and potentially secure two historic LA28 Olympic berths.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'You can't let the Olympic spot go by so quickly': Anahat Singh's stunning admission after 0-2 comeback
articles.summary: Indian teenager Anahat Singh produced a remarkable comeback against Japan’s higher-ranked Satomi Watanabe to reach the women’s singles final at the Asian
articles.body: Indian teenager Anahat Singh produced a remarkable comeback against Japan’s higher-ranked Satomi Watanabe to reach the women’s singles final at the Asian Games squash event on Saturday, while Abhay Singh also booked his place in the men’s singles title clash.Anahat and Abhay are now one win away from securing a spot at the 2028 Olympics, with the Asian Games men’s and women’s singles gold medallists earning direct qualification for the Games.The 18-year-old Anahat pulled off the biggest win of her career as she recovered from a two-game deficit to defeat world No. 6 Satomi 3-2 in a thrilling 51-minute semifinal at the Nagoya Kinjo-Futo Arena.Anahat won 9-11, 11-13, 12-10, 11-6, 11-3, exacting revenge for her previous five-game defeat against the Japanese player."The last time she won, I was 2-0 up and I ended up losing. And I mean, it was the other way around this time," Anahat said after the match.The prospect of an Olympic qualification spot was also on Anahat's mind as she fought her way back into the contest after falling two games behind."I do focus on that. It's something that I think of it more like something that's motivating rather than pressure. When I was losing, the first thought that came into my mind was you can't let the Olympic spot go by so quickly and you really need to push for it. That's what kept replaying in my head over and over and I think that's something that motivates me rather than pressure that you are supposed to be in the Olympics," Anahat said.Anahat had looked close to defeat after losing the opening two games. She had managed to draw level at 6-6 in the first before Satomi moved ahead and eventually closed it out 11-9.The second game followed a similar pattern. Anahat fought back from behind to level the score at 10-10 and then moved to 11-10, but Satomi responded strongly to win the next three points and take the game 13-11.The Indian then produced the turnaround that changed the match.Trailing 8-10 in the third game, Anahat won four straight points to take it 12-10. She carried that momentum into the fourth, where she again recovered from an early deficit to make it 6-6 before putting together five consecutive points to force a decider.Anahat's control, precision and well-executed drops continued to trouble Satomi, who struggled to regain the momentum she had established early in the match.The deciding game was largely one-way traffic. Anahat dominated the exchanges, produced at least three fine drops and capitalised on a series of unforced errors from Satomi to complete the comeback.The semifinal was briefly interrupted after the two players collided during the second game, with Anahat receiving medical attention."I bit my tongue. So it was bleeding, nothing serious," she said.Anahat, the junior world champion, will face Malaysia’s world No. 5 Sivasangari Subramaniam in Sunday’s final. Sivasangari defeated Hong Kong’s Chan Sin Yuk in the other semifinal."I still have a match left. If I end up playing the number one seed, she's a great player. I've played her numerous times before. I'm just excited to get on the court and see what I can do," said the junior world champion.Abhay sets up Malaysia clashAbhay Singh, meanwhile, had a relatively easier route to the final as he defeated Pakistan’s Muhammad Irfan 3-0 in 35 minutes.Abhay won 11-3, 12-10, 11-6 to make the title clash. He had earlier won gold in the men’s team event and bronze in mixed doubles at these Games."It was not an easy one. I think I did well to make it easy, but respect to your opponent. No Asian Games match is going to come easy," Abhay said later.He will take on Malaysia’s NG Eain Yow in Sunday’s final. NG Eain Yow defeated Pakistan’s Zaman Noor in the other semifinal."I think all the people listening to you love the India-Pakistan stuff, but for us it's just another opponent, just another match. Too many people put too much work into us, you have to come in and do them justice."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Assefa vuelve al maratón de Berlín para asaltar un récord mundial bajo 'sospecha'
articles.standfirst: La etíope regresa al escenario de su plusmarca universal de 2023 para intentar batir el posterior registro de 2.09:56 que estableció Chepngetich, ahora suspendida por dopaje
articles.summary: La etíope regresa al escenario de su plusmarca universal en 2023 para acercarse al registro de 2.09:56 que estableció Chepngetich, ahora suspendida por dopaje
articles.body: Tigst Assefa regresa este domingo a las calles de Berlín, donde hace tres años estableció el récord del mundo femenino de maratón, con una marca de 2.11:53. Ahora la etíope es la tercera atleta en el ranking de todos los tiempos, ya que fue superada por su compatriota Tesfay (2.10:51 en Barcelona este año) y la keniata Ruth Chepngetich, ahora suspendida por dopaje, que corrió en 2.09:56 en Chicago en 2024. La subcampeona olímpica y mundial es uno de los grandes focos de esta edición de la carrera alemana, que en categoría masculina había anunciado a Sebastian Sawe, plusmarquista mundial y primer atleta en bajar de las 2.00:00 en maratón, que finalmente es baja por lesión. Tampoco estará al final Kenenisa Bekele, que tenía previsto volver a la capital germana a sus 44 años, pero también se ha lesionado en uno de los últimos entrenamientos. Assefa se erige, por tanto, en la gran favorita y busca su tercer triunfo consecutivo en Berlín. Compite por primera vez desde su victoria en el último maratón de Londres, en el que estableció un récord mundial sólo en carrera de mujeres con un tiempo de 2.15:41 en abril. “Tengo muchas ganas de volver a correr en el rápido circuito de Berlín y espero poder continuar con mi racha de éxitos este domingo”, aseguró. “Estoy muy bien preparada y quiero lograr mi mejor marca personal”. Entre sus rivales, habrá siete mujeres con marcas inferiores 2.20:00. Entre ellas se encuentran la keniana Rosemary Wanjiru, que defiende su título del pasado año, y la etíope Dera Dida, compañera de entrenamiento de Assefa y subcampeona en Berlín el año pasado. Sin Sawe en liza, la carrera masculina se presenta más abierta que nunca. El tanzano Gabriel Geay, con una marca personal de 2.03:00, es el que encabeza la lista de favoritos en Berlín, junto a los etíopes Guye Adola, Shura Kitata y Getaneh Molla. De hecho, Adola buscará recuperar el título que ya ganó en 2021. El atleta de 35 años estableció su mejor marca personal de 2.03:46 en Berlín en 2017, pero estuvo cerca de igualarla al ganar en Rotterdam en abril con un tiempo de 2.03:54. En la lista de participantes también figuran Selemon Barega, campeón olímpico de 10.000 metros en 2021, que terminó séptimo en el maratón de Tokio en marzo (2.05:00), así como el keniano Erick Sang, que corrió en 2.05:34 en la carrera de Rotterdam, ganada por Adola.

articles.title: Lindsey Vonn, French Skiier Matthieu Bailet Reveal Relationship with New Photos from Summer Vacation
articles.summary: Three-time Olympic medalist Lindsey Vonn confirmed her relationship with French skier Matthieu Bailet on social media.
articles.body:
Three-time Olympic medalist Lindsey Vonn confirmed her relationship with French skier Matthieu Bailet on social media.

Vonn posted a series of photos on Instagram this week summing up her summer. She included multiple shots of herself and Bailet together.

The 41-year-old certainly earned the right to have a relaxing break given the ordeal she experienced this past winter. She ruptured her ACL prior to the 2026 Winter Olympics and then suffered a complex leg fracture while competing in the Milan Cortina Games.

Vonn said in August she was still in the recovery phase with another surgery ahead.

articles.title: Olympics: Germany picks Munich for Summer Games bid
articles.summary: Since the last time the Summer Games were on German soil in 1972, Germany has launched seven unsuccessful bids to host.
articles.body:
Munich has been selected ahead of the Cologne/Rhine-Ruhr region by the German Olympic Committee (DOSB) as part of a bid to host the 2036, 2040 or 2044 Olympic Games.

The decision was announced by German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier on Saturday in the southwestern spa town of Baden-Baden.

Launched as a race between four candidates, the DOSB was given a choice between two after Berlin withdrew on Thursday and Hamburg’s withdrawal in May.

“We’re thinking about all of Germany,” Bavarian state premier Markus Soeder said on stage after Munich’s successful bid was announced.

“The Cologne bid made things really tough for us and pretty tense until the end.

“I want that we work jointly to bring the games to Germany. It is a chance at something historic, and we want to give everything to present ourselves as a united country – from north to south and from east to west.

“That’s our goal and what we’re working towards. Thank you for the trust.”

The Munich bid centres on the Olympic Park in the north of the city. Built for the 1972 Games, it has undergone extensive renovations in recent years.

In a statement issued moments after the announcement, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz congratulated Munich.

“Germany has an Olympic candidate. Munich will enter the race on our behalf, and I warmly congratulate the state capital and the Free State of Bavaria on this,” he said.

“Now, together with our Olympic candidate, we eagerly look forward to this major event … Germany is ready for the Olympics.”

In order to shore up support for the bid, Munich held a referendum in late 2025. Almost two-thirds (66.4 percent) of voters cast their ballot in support of hosting the Games, on a turnout of 44 percent.

The positive result was a stark contrast to previous Olympic referenda, with votes to host the 2022 Winter Games in Munich or the 2024 Summer Games in Hamburg failing to win support.

Hamburg’s hopes to be chosen as a potential host city by the DOSB for the 2036, 2040 or 2044 Games were undermined by a negative public consultation, while another hopeful, Berlin, decided against holding a referendum.

The DOSB is set to begin a “continuous dialogue” process with the IOC in the run-up to a shortlisting process in March 2027.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) will designate one or more preferred hosts in late 2028, with an eventual bid to be selected by the IOC in mid 2029.

Since the last time the Summer Games were on German soil in 1972, Germany has launched seven unsuccessful bids to again play host.

If the bid is successfully chosen by the IOC, it will be the third time Germany has hosted the Olympics. Berlin hosted the Games in 1936 with Germany then under Nazi leadership, while Munich played host to the 1972 Games, then as part of West Germany.

The 1972 edition in Munich was marred by the attack on the Israeli delegation in the Olympic Village, which resulted in the deaths of 11 members of the Israeli Olympic team.

The only other Games held on German soil were the 1936 Winter Games, held in the southern town of Garmisch-Partenkirchen.
